title: Adjudicating a British Parliamentary round
intro: Four teams debate the motion “This House would ban private cars from city centres”: Opening and Closing Government for it, Opening and Closing Opposition against. Each of the eight speeches lasts 7 minutes; points of information may be offered only after the first and before the last minute. Three judges ranked the teams on their own; the panel's ranking takes, for each pair of teams, the side most judges preferred (the chair breaks ties), and gives 3, 2, 1 and 0 team points. Predict the panel's rank of each team, then compare. The bars show how long each speech lasted against the 7-minute limit, and the flow sheet shows which arguments were answered.
argA2: Shops in the centre will lose customers
argA3: Footfall rises when streets are pedestrianised
argA4: Free public transport pays for itself
argA6: Congestion already costs more than the subsidy
consLabel: Every ballot agrees with its speaker points
otLabel: Time of the DLO beyond 7 minutes
protLabel: Points of information offered in protected time
dropLabel: Arguments the other side never answered
flowTitle: Flow of the round: who answered what
